terms.definition: Agentic AI refers to systems that transition from passive chat interfaces to autonomous actors capable of multi-step reasoning, planning, and tool utilization. These systems use iterative feedback loops to execute complex workflows across disparate software environments without constant human intervention.
terms.analogy: In a car, standard AI is the GPS giving you directions; Agentic AI is the self-driving system that actually operates the steering wheel, pedals, and signals to get you to your destination while navigating traffic in real-time.
terms.business_value: This shifts AI from a 'consultant' to a 'digital employee,' allowing for the automation of end-to-end operational processes like debt collection or software deployment, which reduces headcount dependency and dramatically increases execution speed.

terms.definition: This process involves capturing multimodal data—such as spatial movements, haptic pressure, and visual sequences—from humans performing physical tasks to train 'world models' for robotics. By digitizing chores and manual labor, developers enable humanoid robots to learn the physics and nuances required to operate in unstructured human environments.
terms.analogy: Think of a kitchen where you aren't just reading a recipe, but actually recording the precise pressure a chef applies to a knife and the exact angle of a pan toss. You are turning 'muscle memory' into a digital blueprint that any robotic arm can download.
terms.business_value: It represents the bridge between digital intelligence and physical labor; for CEOs, this means the eventual automation of high-churn manual roles in logistics, facility maintenance, and hospitality through scalable robotic fleets.

terms.definition: Algorithmic Alignment is the technical discipline of ensuring an AI model’s goals and behaviors remain strictly within the bounds of human ethics and safety protocols. It utilizes techniques like Constitutional AI or Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) to prevent 'reward hacking,' where an agent might achieve a goal through unintended or harmful shortcuts.
terms.analogy: Imagine a kitchen blender programmed only to 'make a smoothie as fast as possible.' Without alignment, it might blend your jewelry if it's nearby to add volume. Alignment is the safety governor that ensures the blender only operates on food, regardless of the speed requirement.
terms.business_value: As AI gains autonomy, alignment becomes the ultimate risk-mitigation tool; it protects the brand from 'hallucinated' liabilities and ensures that autonomous agents don't violate regulatory or ethical standards while pursuing bottom-line targets.
